transcript.text: my tumble dryer is giving off a burning smell?? is it safe to keep using it

No — stop using it immediately. A burning smell from a tumble dryer can indicate overheating lint, an electrical fault, a slipping belt, or a failing motor, all of which can be a fire risk.

1. Turn it off and unplug it (or switch it off at the wall/circuit breaker).
• If it’s a gas dryer, turn off the gas supply too if you can safely do so.
2. Do not run another cycle “to see if it clears.”
3. If you see smoke, flames, sparking, or the smell is strong/persistent, move away from it and call emergency services/fire service. Don’t open panels or pour water on an electrical appliance.
4. Once fully cool and unplugged, you can safely check and clean:
• the lint filter,
• the area around/behind the dryer,
• the vent hose and outside vent flap for lint blockage or crushing.
5. If the smell happened despite a clean filter/vent, or it smells like burning plastic/rubber/electrics, arrange for an appliance technician to inspect it before using it again.

Even a lint blockage can make the dryer overheat, so it’s not safe to keep using until the cause is found.

ok I've switched it off at the wall after the second time it happened?? the lint filter is really full, haven't cleaned it in a few weeks. the hose behind looks squashed with fluff in the end of it. is that what caused it??

A blocked lint filter and a squashed, fluff-filled hose are very plausible causes: they restrict airflow, so the dryer overheats and lint can scorch. But you can’t safely assume that’s the only issue, especially since it has happened twice.

Keep it switched off and unplugged until you’ve dealt with it.

Once it is fully cool:

• Remove and thoroughly clean the lint filter. If it has a film from fabric softener/detergent, wash it with warm water and a soft brush, then let it dry completely.
• Carefully remove lint from the hose and the dryer’s vent outlet. Vacuum is better than pushing lint farther down the pipe.
• Check the whole hose for crushing, kinks, splits, or heavy lint buildup. Straighten/reposition it; replace it if it stays flattened or is damaged.
• Check the external vent flap/outlet, if it vents outdoors, and clear any lint there too.
• Vacuum lint from behind and underneath the dryer.

Do not run it again if you still smell burning, if it got unusually hot, if there was smoke, or if the hose/plug/cable looks damaged. In that case, arrange an appliance repair technician. Also get it checked if the smell returns even after the airflow path is completely cleaned—there could be an electrical, belt, motor, or heating-element problem.

For future use, clean the lint filter after every load, and inspect/clean the vent hose regularly.
